• Scientific name: Pseudecheneis sulcata (McClelland, 1842)
  • Common name: Brahmaputra Suckerthroat
  • Type locality: Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, India
  • Sexing: not known
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2009)
Asia: India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Reported from Tibet and Myanmar.
Found in fast-flowing hill streams. Prefers deep riffles and runs over gravel and cobble substrates.
Unreported in the aquarium. There is no breeding report.

Fishes of the genus Pseudecheneis can be differentiated from other Glyptosternine fish in having a thoracic adhesive apparatus consisting of a series of transverse ridges (laminae) separated by grooves (sulcae).

Pseudecheneis sulcata can be distinguished from congeners by a unique combination of characters, including the lack of a prominent bony spur on the anterodorsal surface of the first dorsal-fin pterygiophore, separate pelvic fins, a less convex snout when viewed laterally, presence of pale spots on the body, 36–39 vertebrae and 12–14 transverse laminae on the thoracic adhesive apparatus.
